extracted.intended_audience: graduate and advanced undergraduate students and researchers in algebraic topology
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions, theorems, and methods concerning fiber bundles, (Serre) fibrations, and the long exact sequence of homotopy groups, with examples (Hopf bundles, Stiefel/Grassmann manifolds) and constructions used to compute homotopy groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiber bundle (local triviality) definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A fiber bundle structure on a space E, with fiber F, consists of a projection map p : E→B such that each point of B has a neighborhood U for which there is a homeomorphism h : p^{-1}(U)→U × F making the diagram commute; h carries each fiber F_b = p^{-1}(b) homeomorphically onto the copy {b}×F of F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local trivialization h is determined by its second coordinate (a map p^{-1}(U)→F which is a homeomorphism on each fiber). Examples: product bundle F×B with projection, the Möbius band (interval fiber over S^1), Klein bottle (circle fiber over S^1), projective-space bundles (S^{2n+1}→CP^n with S^1 fibers). The bundle is often denoted F→E→B and B is called the base, E the total space.

rubrics_metrics.name: Homotopy lifting property (HLP) definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A map p : E→B has the homotopy lifting property with respect to a space X if, given a homotopy g_t : X→B and a map g_0 : X→E lifting g_0 (i.e. p∘g_0 = g_0), there exists a homotopy tilde{g}_t : X→E lifting g_t.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formally this is a special case of the lift extension property for a pair (Z,A). The case (Z,A)=(X×I, X×{0}) is the homotopy lifting property. Relative version: HLP for a pair (X,A) means each homotopy f_t : X→B lifts to g_t : X→E extending a given lift on A; equivalently the lift extension property for (X×I, X×{0}∪A×I).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fibration / Serre fibration
rubrics_metrics.description: A fibration is a map p : E→B having the homotopy lifting property with respect to all spaces X. A map p satisfying the homotopy lifting property for disks D^k for all k≥0 is sometimes called a Serre fibration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projection B×F→B is a (trivial) fibration (choose lifts of form (g_t(x), h(x))). The homotopy lifting property for disks is equivalent to the HLP for all CW pairs, and hence to HLP for all CW pairs by cellular induction (subdivide by skeleta).

rubrics_metrics.name: Condition for long exact sequence of homotopy groups (Theorem 4.41)
rubrics_metrics.description: If p : E→B has the homotopy lifting property with respect to disks D^k for all k≥0, then p_* : π_n(E, F, x_0)→π_n(B, b_0) is an isomorphism for all n≥1. If B is path-connected, there is a long exact sequence ...→π_n(F,x_0)→π_n(E,x_0)→π_n(B,b_0)→π_{n-1}(F,x_0)→...→π_0(E,x_0)→0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses relative HLP and cellular induction; surjectivity is by lifting a representative map on the disk relative to a skeleton, injectivity by lifting homotopies. The trailing 0 comes from surjectivity of π_0(F)→π_0(E) when B is path-connected (path-lift argument).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiber bundles are fibrations (Proposition 4.48)
rubrics_metrics.description: A fiber bundle p : E→B has the homotopy lifting property with respect to all CW pairs (X,A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof strategy: choose open cover {U_α} of B with local trivializations h_α : p^{-1}(U_α)→U_α×F; using compactness of the domain (e.g., I^n×I) subdivide so each small cube maps into a single U_α, reduce to product case where lift exists by composing with a retraction and given data. Huebsch–Hurewicz theorem (Spanier) strengthens this: fiber bundles over paracompact bases are fibrations (HLP for all spaces).

rubrics_metrics.name: Serre fibration criterion (equivalence for disks and CW pairs)
rubrics_metrics.description: The homotopy lifting property for D^k is equivalent to the homotopy lifting property for the pair (D^k, ∂D^k), and thus equivalent to the HLP for all CW pairs; hence HLP for disks characterizes Serre fibrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pairs (D^k×I, D^k×{0}) and (D^k×I, D^k×{0}∪∂D^k×I) are homeomorphic, enabling reduction; lifting over skeleta reduces to disk case via characteristic maps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local-triviality check by explicit charts
rubrics_metrics.description: To show a map p : E→B is a fiber bundle with fiber F, exhibit for each b∈B a neighborhood U and an explicit homeomorphism h : p^{-1}(U)→U×F sending fibers to {b}×F (i.e., give local trivializations and inverses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show construction: for S^{2n+1}→CP^n take Ui={classes with z_i≠0} and define h_i(z)=([z], z_i/|z_i|) with explicit inverse; for Hopf bundles define projection formulas in polar coordinates and analyze fiber tori. Verifying h and its inverse are mutual homeomorphisms (often by explicit algebraic formulas) is the standard method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Covering spaces as discrete-fiber bundles
rubrics_metrics.description: A fiber bundle with discrete fiber is a covering space. Conversely, a covering space whose fibers all have the same cardinality (e.g., over a connected base) is a fiber bundle with discrete fiber.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applying Theorem 4.41 to a covering space p : E→B with E,B path-connected yields p_* : π_n(E)→π_n(B) is an isomorphism for n≥2 and a short exact sequence 0→π_1(E)→π_1(B)→π_0(F)→0; fiber can be identified with cosets of p_*π_1(E) in π_1(B) via path-lifting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using fibration LES to compute homotopy groups (method)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a fibration F→E→B and knowledge/vanishing of π_i of fiber or total space in certain ranges, use the long exact sequence of homotopy groups to deduce isomorphisms and compute unknown π_i groups (e.g., π_2(S^2)≈π_1(S^1) from Hopf bundle).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Hopf bundle S^1→S^3→S^2 gives π_2(S^2)≈π_1(S^1) and π_i(S^3)≈π_i(S^2) for i≥3 because π_i(S^1)=0 for i>1 and π_i(S^3) vanishes in certain adjacent terms. For contractible total space (e.g., S^∞) one gets π_i(CP^∞)≈π_{i-1}(S^1) etc; use vanishing/isomorphism adjacencies in the exact sequence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative homotopy lifting property and identification π_n(E,F)→π_n(B)
rubrics_metrics.description: The relative HLP for pairs (X,A) lets one lift maps (I^n,∂I^n,J^{n−1})→(B,b_0) to lifts (I^n,∂I^n,J^{n−1})→(E,F,x_0) and thereby show p_* : π_n(E,F,x_0)→π_n(B,b_0) is an isomorphism under HLP-for-disks hypotheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof constructs lifts cell-by-cell (skeleton induction) and uses permutations of coordinates in In×I to extend partial lifts to full lifts; injectivity and surjectivity arguments are symmetric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whitehead product construction and properties
rubrics_metrics.description: Given basepoint-preserving maps f : S^k→X and g : S^ℓ→X, the Whitehead product [f,g]: S^{k+ℓ−1}→X is the composition S^{k+ℓ−1}→S^k∨S^ℓ→X where the first map is the attaching map of the (k+ℓ)–cell of S^k×S^ℓ; defines a product π_k(X)×π_ℓ(X)→π_{k+ℓ−1}(X) and for k=ℓ=1 recovers the commutator in π_1(X).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whitehead products arise as attaching maps in CW constructions (e.g., π_3 of a wedge of S^2's has basis of Whitehead products). For k=1 and ℓ>1, [f,g] measures difference between g and its image under π_1 action by f.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction and local-triviality of Stiefel/Grassmann bundles
rubrics_metrics.description: The projection p : V_n(R^k)→G_n(R^k) sending an n-frame to the n-plane it spans is a fiber bundle with fiber V_n(R^n) ≈ O(n); local trivializations are produced by choosing an orthonormal basis for a plane P and projecting that basis orthogonally onto nearby planes, then applying Gram–Schmidt continuously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complex and quaternionic analogs use Hermitian/ quaternionic inner products; direct limit k→∞ yields V_n(R^∞)=⋃_k V_n(R^k) and Gn(R^∞)=⋃_k Gn(R^k). Connectivity facts follow from fibration LES applied inductively: V_n(R^k) is (k−n−1)-connected, complex and quaternionic analogues have stated connectivities, and V_n(R^∞) etc. are contractible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bundles arising from frames: V_{n−m}(R^{k−m})→V_n(R^k)→V_m(R^k)
rubrics_metrics.description: For m<n≤k the projection sending an n-frame to its first m vectors gives a fiber bundle whose fiber is (n−m)-frames in the (k−m)-plane orthogonal to that m-frame; local trivializations constructed by choosing orthonormal bases and applying Gram–Schmidt continuously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special case m=1 yields bundles V_{n−1}(R^{k−1})→V_n(R^k)→S^{k−1} used to inductively deduce connectivity statements. Similar constructions hold in complex and quaternionic cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coset-space descriptions of frame/Grassmann manifolds
rubrics_metrics.description: One can identify V_m(R^k) with the coset space O(k)/O(k−m) (fibers as right cosets αO(k−m)) and G_m(R^k) with O(k)/(O(m)×O(k−m)), where O(m)×O(k−m) is the subgroup fixing the chosen m-plane.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analogous identifications hold for unitary and symplectic groups in the complex and quaternionic cases; these identifications explain homogeneous-space structure and free actions by subgroups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stability and Bott periodicity for classical groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusions O(n−1)→O(n), U(n−1)→U(n), Sp(n−1)→Sp(n) induce isomorphisms on π_i for i < n−2 (real case) so π_i of these groups stabilize for large n. Bott periodicity: the stable groups repeat periodically (period 8 for O and Sp, period 2 for U) and their stable values are tabulated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bundles O(n−1)→O(n)→S^{n−1} etc. provide LES to deduce stability. The text provides a table of stable homotopy groups (i mod 8 rows) illustrating periodicity; these are fundamental computations in topology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of stable homotopy groups π^s_i(X)
rubrics_metrics.description: The stable homotopy group π^s_i(X) is the eventual value of iterated suspensions π_{i+n}(Σ^n X) once suspension maps become isomorphisms; for spheres π^s_i denotes the stable homotopy groups of spheres (π_{i+n}(S^n) for sufficiently large n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corollary: suspension is isomorphism for i<2n+1 when X is n-connected; Serre's theorem: π^s_i(S^0) (stable stem) is finite for i>0. Calculations known up to finite ranges; further structure studied via p-primary (p-component) decompositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: p-component decomposition and p-adic 'ruler' families
rubrics_metrics.description: For studying π^s_* one often project to p-components (elements of order a power of p). For each prime p there are infinite 'p-adic rulers'—infinite families of cyclic subgroups of order p^{m+1} in certain dimensions (e.g., dimensions 2j(p−1)−1), giving systematic families in pπ^s_* (Im J phenomena etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diagrams for p=2,3,5 illustrate vertical Z_{2^n} or Z_{p^n} summands and 'teeth'/'rulers' patterns; some potential elements remain conjectural (question marks in diagrams).

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition products and graded-commutative ring structure (Proposition 4.56)
rubrics_metrics.description: The composition products π^s_i × π^s_j → π^s_{i+j} induce a graded ring structure on π^s_* satisfying αβ = (−1)^{ij} βα for α∈π^s_i and β∈π^s_j.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses smash-product interpretation of suspension (S^n ∧ S^k ≅ S^{n+k}) and sign computations from transpositions of circle factors (degree signs). Distributivity and graded-commutativity follow from these identifications and parity arguments on permutations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Toda brackets as higher-order composition constructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Given maps f:W→X, g:X→Y, h:Y→Z with gf and hg null-homotopic, one defines the Toda bracket ⟨f,g,h⟩ : ΣW→Z by extending null-homotopies and gluing on cones; the bracket depends on choices and ranges over a coset of a subgroup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Toda brackets (and higher-order brackets) produce many of the elements in stable stems and are used to express elements in terms of brackets; in diagrams dashed lines often indicate bracket relationships. Non-uniqueness and indeterminacy are important and described in exercises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method: prove HLP for fiber bundles by reduction to product case
rubrics_metrics.description: To prove a fiber bundle has HLP for a given domain (e.g., In×I), cover B by trivializing neighborhoods, use compactness to subdivide domain so each small cell maps into one trivializing neighborhood, then reduce to product bundle case where lifts are constructed using retraction and given boundary data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the standard proof (used in Proposition 4.48): after subdivision, compose the given partial lift with the local trivialization to reduce to U×F and extend the lift by constructing the second-coordinate map using retractions onto boundary and the given maps into F.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connectivity consequences from fibrations (applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: Using bundles V_{n−1}(R^{k−1})→V_n(R^k)→S^{k−1} and LES of homotopy groups one can deduce connectivity statements: V_n(R^k) is (k−n−1)-connected, V_n(C^k) is (2k−2n) connected, V_n(H^k) is (4k−4n+2)-connected; infinite versions V_n(R^∞), V_n(C^∞), V_n(H^∞) are contractible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inductive use of the LES for the fiber bundles V_{n−1}→V_n→S^{k−1} establishes connectivity; contractibility of V_n(R^∞) given by explicit deformation retractions using linear homotopies plus Gram–Schmidt.
